stem:
Navya tosses a pebble straight up from a terrace. The pebble rises more slowly, stops for a moment, then falls and speeds up on the way down.

Which claim correctly explains the motion?

options.text: Earth pulls the pebble toward itself the whole time, so the pebble slows going up and speeds up coming down.
The pebble carries an upward force from the toss until that force runs out; Earth pulls only after the pebble starts falling.
An object tossed upward speeds up until it leaves Earth.
Earth pushes the pebble upward while the pebble rises.

teacher.key_rationale: Earth's gravitational pull acts toward Earth without contact throughout the flight, so the pebble slows while rising and speeds up while falling. An upward force does not stay inside until it runs out; the pebble does not speed up leaving Earth; Earth does not push it upward while it rises.
